rationale: John also places the walk on the sea right after the feeding of the five thousand. Jesus withdraws "to a mountain by Himself" (6:15), the disciples cross in the dark against "A strong wind" (6:18), they see Him "walking on the sea" and are "terrified" (6:19), and He says, "It is I; do not be afraid" (6:20, BSB). The type is parallel and the label strong, not explicit, following conn-matt12-family-mark3: neither Gospel cites the other. The differences can be checked. John gives a reason for the withdrawal that Matthew does not, that the crowd was "about to come and make Him king by force" (6:15), and a distance, "about three or four miles" (6:19). John's saying has no "Take courage" (in the Greek editions read, no tharseite), only egō eimi, mē phobeisthe. John has no Peter episode and no worship or confession in the boat; instead, "at once the boat reached the shore where they were heading" (6:21, BSB). Luke has no account of the walk on the sea at all, as Augustine already noted (Harmony of the Gospels II.47).
